name: Range
author: unknown

provenance.note: No documentation or author attribution found on the disc.
provenance.redistribution: Third-party extension, redistribution terms unverified. The AMOS PD Library on CD (Weird Science, 1994), archive.org item cdrom-amospdcd. The disc's own Documents/Copyrights states Weird Science claims no copyright over the material, that parts are shareware with fees due, and that users should make no assumption that anything on it is public domain. Kept as a fixture for identification and reference only.

findings: Version CORRECTED off the binary: the title string at $ffd is `AMOS Club Extension V2.6`, where this manifest recorded 2.8 from Andrew Burton's AMOS Extensions List; the id keeps its original spelling. Slot 9 off the binary too, twice: routine 0 does `move.l a3,$178(a5)` and returns `moveq #$8,d0`. This build has no 'APex' guard, so it is the AMOS 1.3 one. Its 52 token entries are byte-identical to the first 52 of range-2.0's, ids, specs and routine numbers alike, so ONE port serves both — see src/runtime/range.ts. A four-keyword shuffle.lib on APD426 contains a subset (range, shuffle, rand) and is an earlier build of the same extension rather than a separate one; it is not registered separately.
notes: Version 2.6 fallback for the AMOS Club extension.
